days.title: Eastern Peaks and Border Valleys
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Botrange
stops.detail: The highest elevation is the Botrange in the province of Liège at 694 m above the Ostend reference level.

stops.name: Baraque de Fraiture
stops.detail: The highest elevation attributable only to the Ardennes is the Baraque de Fraiture in the north of the province of Luxembourg (Belgium) at 652 m above sea level.

stops.name: Tal der Our
stops.detail: South of there, the Our Valley can be seen as the border between the Eifel and the Ardennes.

days.title: Northern Valleys and Gorges
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Durchbruchstal der Maas
stops.detail: The most significant Ardennes valley is the Meuse Gorge between Charleville-Mézières and Namur, particularly deeply carved between Charleville and Dinant.

stops.name: Tal der Sambre
stops.detail: The northern boundary of the Ardennes is the Sambre Valley and the subsequent section of the Meuse Valley between Namur and Liège.

days.title: Southwestern Ridges and Hills
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Crêtes Préardennaises
stops.detail: This includes extensive high forests (300 to almost 400 m) near the Meuse west of Fumay as well as the Crêtes Préardennaises (Ridges of the Pre-Ardennes), which extend south of the Sedan – Charleville-Mézières – Hirson line predominantly in an east-west direction, belong to the Northern French scarp lands and feature much agriculture and pasture alongside forest, a hedgerow landscape (Bocage).

stops.name: Collines de la Thiérache
stops.detail: West of the confluence of the Gland and the Oise near Hirson, the Collines de la Thiérache (Thiérache Hills) are included, extending to the furrow used for the Canal de la Sambre à l'Oise.
